page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-30 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 30 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 15 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 120.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI, though it lacks Advanced Matrix Extensions and local NVMe storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-core performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 2862.37 and a PassMark memory score of 2761.2, both placing in the top 25%. Multi-core execution and memory read bandwidth remain within average parameters, with a PassMark CPU score of 41531.46 and a large-block read bandwidth of 71.86 GB/sec. However, a notable performance bottleneck exists in large-block memory write operations, which register at a weak 25.49 GB/sec. Similarly, while text generation for small 135M LLM models is strong at 328.85 tokens/sec, prompt processing for large 70B models drops to a weak 7.43 tokens/sec due to the lack of hardware GPU acceleration.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c3d-standard-30 offers a balanced resource density suitable for general-purpose enterprise workloads that do not require local SSD storage or dedicated GPUs. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this instance appropriate for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database operations, and static web serving. It is also suitable for lightweight machine learning inference on smaller models, though workloads requiring heavy write operations or massive LLM execution may encounter resource constraints.
